**Australia**, officially the **Commonwealth of Australia**, is a country comprising the [mainland](/wiki/Mainland_Australia "Mainland Australia") of the [Australian continent](/wiki/Australia_(continent) "Australia (continent)"), the island of [Tasmania](/wiki/Tasmania "Tasmania") and [numerous smaller islands](/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Australia "List of islands of Australia").[[N 6]](#cite_note-22) It has a land area of 7,688,287 km2 (2,968,464 sq mi), making it the [sixth-largest country in the world](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area"). Australia is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent. It is a [megadiverse country](/wiki/Megadiverse_countries "Megadiverse countries"), and its size gives it a wide variety of landscapes and [climates](/wiki/Climate_of_Australia "Climate of Australia") including [deserts](/wiki/Deserts_of_Australia "Deserts of Australia") in the [interior](/wiki/Outback "Outback") and [tropical rainforests](/wiki/Forests_of_Australia "Forests of Australia") along the [coast](/wiki/Eastern_states_of_Australia "Eastern states of Australia").

Essential amino acid :: Amino acid requirements and the amino acid content of food :: part 01 :: chunk_0005
Historically, amino acid requirements were determined by calculating the balance between dietary [nitrogen](/wiki/Nitrogen "Nitrogen") intake and nitrogen excreted in the liquid and solid wastes, because proteins represent the largest nitrogen content in a body. A positive balance occurs when more nitrogen is consumed than is excreted, which indicates that some of the nitrogen is being used by the body to build proteins. A negative nitrogen balance occurs when more nitrogen is excreted than is consumed, which indicates that there is insufficient intake for the body to maintain its health. Graduate students at the [University of Illinois](/wiki/University_of_Illinois "University of Illinois") were fed an artificial diet so that there was a slightly positive nitrogen balance. Then one amino acid was omitted and the nitrogen balance recorded. If a positive balance continued, then that amino acid was deemed not essential. If a negative balance occurred, then that amino acid was slowly restored until a slightly positive nitrogen balance stabilized and the minimum amount recorded.[[17]](#cite_note-RoseIsoleucine-17)[[18]](#cite_note-McGilvery1979-18)

A similar method was used to determine the protein content of foods. Test subjects were fed a diet containing no protein and the nitrogen losses recorded. During the first week or more there is a rapid loss of [labile](/wiki/Lability "Lability") proteins. Once the nitrogen losses stabilize, this baseline is determined to be the minimum required for maintenance. Then the test subjects were fed a measured amount of the food being tested. The difference between the nitrogen in that food and the nitrogen losses above baseline was the amount the body retained to rebuild proteins. Capitol Records, from December 1963 when it began issuing Beatles recordings for the US market, exercised complete control over format,[[90]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewisohn1992350-92) compiling distinct US albums from the band's recordings and issuing songs of their choosing as singles.[[174]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGould2007295–296-180)[[nb 7]](#cite_note-182) In June 1966, the Capitol LP *[Yesterday and Today](/wiki/Yesterday_and_Today "Yesterday and Today")* caused an uproar with its cover, which portrayed the grinning Beatles dressed in butcher's overalls, accompanied by raw meat and mutilated plastic baby dolls. According to Beatles biographer [Bill Harry](/wiki/Bill_Harry "Bill Harry"), it has been incorrectly suggested that this was meant as a satirical response to the way Capitol had "butchered" the US versions of the band's albums.[[176]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarry2000a1187-183) Thousands of copies of the LP had a new cover pasted over the original; an unpeeled "first-state" copy fetched $10,500 at a December 2005 auction.[[177]](#cite_note-184) In England, meanwhile, Harrison met sitar maestro [Ravi Shankar](/wiki/Ravi_Shankar "Ravi Shankar"), who agreed to train him on the instrument.[[178]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELavezzoli2006176-185)

The Beatles toured Japan the month after the *Yesterday and Today* furore, facing death threats from Japanese Conservatives due to the Beatles unknowingly performing at the [Budokan Stadium](/wiki/Nippon_Budokan "Nippon Budokan"), which was designated as a place to revere Japan's war dead. With a diameter of about 5,270 kilometres (3,270 mi) and a mass of 1.48×1020 tonnes (1.48×1023 kg; 3.26×1023 lb), Ganymede is the largest and most massive [moon](/wiki/Satellite_system_(astronomy) "Satellite system (astronomy)") in the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System").[[46]](#cite_note-55) It is slightly more massive than the second most massive moon, Saturn's satellite [Titan](/wiki/Titan_(moon) "Titan (moon)"), and is more than twice as massive as the Earth's Moon. Ganymede is the ninth-largest object in the solar system, but the tenth-most massive.
